transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-07 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Mark (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Tom A. (Polaris Head ML), Sana R. (Infra), Jules P. (Product)

Summary: quick triage of week-2 pilot numbers, focused on latency spike during 95th/99th percentile and throughput under burst load vs incumbent. Action items and routing/playbook next steps agreed.

[00:00] Mark (Redwood): all right everybody, thanks for joining the sync, uh we wanted to kick off with the quick TLDR on the bench comparisons you ran overnight vs the incumbent. Priya and I looked at the dashboards this morning.

[01:12] Tom (Polaris): yeah thanks Mark. First off, appreciate the help getting the load harness up. We saw lower average latency on Redwood at baseline prompt length, but the 99th is still worse in sustained bursts, which is kinda the main blocker for product SLOs.

[02:43] Priya (Redwood): right, so average is down about 18% and p50/p90 look great, but the p99 tail during our 2k rps bursts went up about 30% vs the incumbent. I think two things are colliding: the routing policy sent too many mid-size requests into the quantized variant, and the KV cache hit rate dropped during the run.

[04:10] Sana (Polaris): re KV cache, our tracing shows a drop from 72% to 41% hit rate around minute 22 of the run, that lines up with the tail. Could be request variance. Also curious on the batching size you used — we defaulted to 32 but maybe your runtime optimizations prefer smaller for low-latency hedging?

[05:35] Priya (Redwood): good point. For that run we left auto-batching on with a max batch of 48 to maximize throughput. We can tweak it — suggest trying continuous batching with max 24 and lower latency‑first policy so it favors lower batch depth when queue latency rises. That usually helps tail.

[07:00] Jules (Polaris): could that increase per-token cost though? Our CFO is watching.

[07:18] Mark (Redwood): yes tradeoff exists. Lower batch size increases per-token compute inefficiency, so cost rises. But our optimize toolkit suggests that for your workload the delta is ~6-8% for p99 reduction of ~20-25% — we'll send the exact spreadsheet.

[08:45] Tom: under load, we also hit a few failed token streams, small number but correlated to the fallback policy kicking in. Can you remind us how that fallback works? Seems like requests were re-routed to a smaller model variant which blew out latency.

[09:32] Priya: fallback routing is time-based — if a slot isn't available within 200ms we route to a compatible variant to preserve throughput. In your config we had 'cost-aware' fallback enabled which prefers cheaper variants; we should flip to 'latency-first' and add a canary slot so critical traffic doesn't fall back.

[10:50] Sana: flipping fallback makes sense. Also need to know about Private VPC constraints — if we move to a dedicated slot will network egress add jitter? Our infra uses an internal NAT and peering; we can share topology.

[11:22] Mark: network jitter is possible but small for our dedicated pools in your region. Priya can work with you to run a simple ping/RTT and a small HTTP load test from your VPC to the dedicated endpoint. If you want, we can include HSM/KMS notes for key management — that'll be in the security doc.

[13:05] Tom: ok. Another observation: the incumbent preserves higher KV cache locality because they keep longer prefix windows which helps your prompt patterns. Can Redwood increase cache TTL without hurting memory pressure?

[13:46] Priya: yes we can tune prefix caching TTLs per route; it's a balance with memory on the GPU. For your model size and batch distribution, moving the KV TTL from 5 minutes to 15 seconds isn't ideal — but extending from 5 to 7 minutes may help. We'll run a memory-pressure sim.

[15:30] Jules: on evaluation, product wants to keep the incumbent where latency > 300ms at p99. If Redwood can't meet that consistently we have a hard requirement to keep fallback to incumbent for critical flows.

[16:12] Mark: understood. Our goal is to provide a deterministic playbook so you have SLOs met. We'll propose two modes: 'latency-priority' for critical routes (p99 < 300ms) with higher cost, and 'balanced' for session or background tasks.

[17:45] Sana: what's the recommended dedicated slot size for this workload? We were thinking 4xA100 equivalents but cost might be high.

[18:05] Priya: based on throughput and sequence length median, we recommend starting with 2xH100-equivalent slots with burst pool enabled. That config gives lower p50/p90 and due to better kernel selection will help p99 at a modest cost than 4xA100. We'll detail the GPU profile in the doc.

[19:40] Tom: interesting. Can you also explain the quantization you ran? The overnight run used 4bit quant but we saw some quality diffs on longer generations.

[20:08] Priya: sure — the pilot used ptq-int4 for the cheaper variant; we preserve a float16 canonical for critical calls. 4-bit does sometimes produce a softer repetition pattern on long tails; for your application where completion integrity matters we recommend hybrid: model-variant for short prompts quantized, long prompts routed to fp16. That is what we mean by route-by-length.

[21:45] Jules: ok sounds good. Also can you confirm logging and audit for compliance? We need SOC2 plus detailed per-request audit for the PII redaction flow.

[22:25] Mark: yes SOC2 Type II in our docs; we have per-request metadata and redaction hooks. We'll share the redwood-security.pdf and a short appendix showing redaction flow and retention policy.

[23:55] Tom: back to the numbers — can we go over the raw bench figures again? I pulled the CSV: incumbent average 110ms, p95 210ms, p99 310ms; Redwood avg 90ms, p95 170ms, p99 400ms. Throughput sustained at 1.8k vs incumbent 2.2k for same lat cap.

[25:20] Priya: thanks Tom. Those numbers match our dashboard. The big delta is the p99 spike and sustained throughput under congestion. The root cause we suspect is twofold: routing fallback and KV cache churn. We'll propose a three-step remediation: 1) routing change to latency-first, 2) adjust batch max to 24 with continuous batching, 3) prefix cache TTL bump and tune memory pressure.

[27:00] Mark: and we'll provide a cost impact sheet. Preliminary estimate: switching to latency-first and lower batch increases monthly unit cost ~7-9% but should get p99 into target range. Dedicated slot add-on is a separate line item — we'll price it.

[28:40] Sana: do you have any examples of other customers who moved to dedicated and saw p99 improvements?

[29:05] Priya: yes, we have a case (anonymized) with a med-tech customer where dedicated plus routing changes dropped p99 by 40% while throughput stayed flat. We'll share that anonymized readout.

[30:25] Tom: can we do an exploratory run where we flip routing to latency-first for 24 hours and keep everything else constant? We'll A/B compare against incumbent during the same window.

[31:02] Mark: yes that's the recommended next step. We'll send a runbook. Ideally you run two identical harnesses, one pointed at Redwood with latency-first routing and one to incumbent. Capture the same traces.

[32:30] Jules: any instrumentation changes we need? We currently only collect per-request latency and error code; should we add per-request model-variant tag and batch-depth logging?

[33:05] Priya: add model-variant and batch-depth and KV hit flag. That will make root-cause analysis much easier. We'll provide the snippet for your tracer.

[34:20] Tom: on guardrails, if we flip fallback to latency-first will that drop some cost-savings? We have to balance.

[34:40] Mark: yes cost will increase slightly as more requests hit canonical fp16 variants. We'll show the delta and a few gradients: latency-first, balanced, cost-first. You can map routes to policies.

[36:10] Sana: security note — before we run a dedicated slot we need the SOC2 report plus network architecture, and an initial PTR (penetration test) questionnaire filled.

[36:40] Mark: understood. We'll attach SOC2 and the PTR questionnaire. Security deep-dive scheduled for 2026-04-21 per earlier.

[37:50] Tom: any risk of quantized variant causing hallucination increase? We saw minor oddness at 200+ token generations.

[38:20] Priya: quantization can exacerbate subtle degradation in long-form. That's why we recommend hybrid routing by prompt length and a lightweight eval harness to catch regression. We'll include an eval suite you can run that scores generation integrity on your prompt corpus.

[39:55] Jules: ok great. Let's recap immediate action items and owners.

[40:10] Mark: recap: Redwood sends routing playbook, batch settings, cost spreadsheet, security docs. Polaris runs 24h A/B starting 2026-04-10, collects model-variant, batch-depth, KV hit metrics. Quick check-in next Thursday same time.

[41:02] Sana: confirmed. Also Priya to send the quantization appendix with suggested hybrid rules.

[41:30] Priya: will do. I'll add a short checklist for running the A/B and the tracer snippet.

[42:00] Tom: perfect. One last thing — can we have a low-touch demo of the route-by-length policy in the console? Jules wants to see the UI.

[42:30] Mark: yes I'll spin up a 20-minute demo session and invite Product and you.

[43:05] Jules: thanks everyone.

[43:20] Mark: thanks team, we'll follow up with the docs and runbook today.

[43:35] (end)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-transcriptions: 'KV cache' appeared as 'K V cash' in one segment; speaker labels auto-attributed in a few short overlaps; punctuation normalized lightly for readability.
